summary: RUNNING UNATTENDED (owner offline, cannot be raised). Quick task 260729-2ig is remediating the test-double taxonomy merged as 1d1474b, which a THREE-reviewer acceptance gate rejected. An oracle consult during discussion FALSIFIED a claim the document makes at nine measured sites -- it attributes a five-member framing to Meszaros that the book never states, while the book explicitly states FOUR. Granted the oracle a scoped search capability; two reviewers found it NOT SAFE; reverted. Decisive finding: rg --pre and rg --hostname-bin each execute an arbitrary program and both match an rg prefix, so NO prefix rule can make search read-only -- and the pattern is advisory anyway (verified by probe: an agent with identical syntax ran five unrelated commands including a file-creating redirection)

Both oracle agents corrected WITHOUT any capability change (still Read, Glob): absence-claim doctrine (scope what you certify, name the remainder under the firewall, token-absence is not concept-absence, carry the hedge into structured output), and match-on-substance-not-wording for the reviewer. Subagent-reviewed, three findings applied

Corrected the rg note in the global CLAUDE.md (local config, no git, never pushed). It was wrong twice: ignore rules apply to TRAVERSAL not to an explicitly named root, so the example never needed -uu; and the -uu/-uuu split was misdescribed. Added the traps that DO make a zero untrustworthy (exit 2 looks like absence, line-oriented misses on wrapped/hyphenated text, regex-by-default, curly quotes) plus the rg --pre security fact. All verified first-hand in a controlled lab, not relayed

decisions.decision: SPLIT ruling on argumentative superstructure: repair the two load-bearing arguments, delete the two that only defend the design.
decisions.rationale: Owner-locked. The governing line: argumentation that tells a coach WHAT IT MAY NOT CITE is operational and stays; argumentation that DEFENDS THE DESIGN belongs in CONTEXT.md. Repair the citability rule (split naming-citation from meaning-citation so the recommendation satisfies it) and the ambiguity finding (weaken a falsified universal to a survey). Cut the degree-of-freedom proof and the deliberate-negative intent claim, keeping the owner-verified blank-column fact.

decisions.decision: Both cuts are PURE deletions -- no carry-forward rider needed.
decisions.rationale: Measured during discussion: both cut passages restate, with weaker warrant, claims a later section already carries WITH chapter citations. One of them also misdescribes what that section currently contains, which is a separate defect. The uncited copy is the one that drifted -- it grew an intent inference and a chronology the cited original never needed. General lesson: when one claim lives in two registers, the uncited copy drifts.

decisions.decision: The five-member framing is an ATTRIBUTION ERROR at nine measured sites, not merely an underivable count.
decisions.rationale: Oracle consult, CONFIRMED by end-to-end reads of five parts: the book NEVER states five and explicitly states FOUR in prose, because its rundown folds two members into one bullet. Five is a reading of the hierarchy figure only; counting from the catalog's variations run yields six or nine instead. So the count is attributed to the figure rather than to the author as his framing, the numeral is kept because the figure supports it, and the caveat that his prose says four is ADDED -- that caveat is exactly the what-you-may-not-cite content this document should carry. Same defect class as the fabricated mapping this remediation exists to remove, repeated nine times.

decisions.decision: The mis-levelling is ONE CELL, not a table restructure.
decisions.rationale: The consult reported four table rows are non-members (an umbrella and three variations), which sounded like it needed a level column or a table split -- trap-quadrant, since it would ripple through every cell bullet, every derived count and the guard work. MEASUREMENT showed the document's convention is to state the relationship in the defining-property cell and it already does so for THREE of the four. Only one row lacks it. Fix that cell; change no table structure. Also measured: the other families the consult warned might be flattened have ZERO rows and ZERO mentions, and the alias collision it flagged is not live here.

decisions.decision: No search capability for either oracle agent; a sweep is the driver's or harness's job.
decisions.rationale: Reviewed NOT SAFE. rg --pre and rg --hostname-bin each run an arbitrary program and both match an rg prefix, so no prefix rule can preserve read-only; the frontmatter pattern is advisory regardless. Granting it would move writes-nothing from a tool-layer guarantee to a promise, in the one agent trusted to hold copyrighted text and whose own threat model anticipates injected instructions inside that text. Two further reasons: the low-leak forms recommended (-c/-l) are precisely a compilation dump, since store filenames are numbered descriptive slugs that together render the table of contents; and the sibling gate requires negatives confirmed by complete read, so sweep-certified absences would stall its converge-to-clean loop. The sibling's own contract already assigns deterministic checks to the harness.

unresolved_cannot_be_raised.item: The numeral-absence claim cannot be certified book-wide this round.
unresolved_cannot_be_raised.detail: The consult's negative is correctly scoped to the parts it read end to end; it declined to sweep the remainder and rightly called a whole-book token sweep a harness job. The oracle has no search tool and the orchestrator is firewalled from the store, so neither can close it. Does NOT block the fix: the figure is the basis for the numeral regardless of any unread chapter, and the prose demonstrably states four. Recorded at the scope actually swept.

unresolved_cannot_be_raised.item: The axis-2 classification of two terms deliberately left out of the table.
unresolved_cannot_be_raised.detail: HIGH impact (would add rows and move cell populations) and NOT high confidence (contested on the merits -- the unprimed reviewer holds both contradict the axis definition). Trap quadrant, so NOT auto-decided. Safe default taken instead: do not add rows; they remain caveats in a later section where they are already cited, which needs no ruling.

next_action: Await the planner, then run the plan-checker loop (max 2 iterations), then dispatch the executor in an isolated worktree with the instrument-first discipline. The acceptance review after execution is the gate, NOT the battery.
context_notes: PROCESS LESSONS THAT KEEP PAYING. Instrument-first with proven-red guards caught the previous executor's own author reproducing banned phrasing verbatim. Reviewers briefed from scratch keep finding what primed ones miss -- the wholly unprimed reviewer found the most this round, including two blocking defects neither other reviewer saw. And an oracle that REFUSES to certify what it did not read is worth more than one that answers: this round's consult overturned the premise it was given, and separately corrected me when I briefed it with a self-contradiction that did not exist (I had matched on the SITE rather than on the WORD -- the document was right and I was wrong). MY OWN ERRORS THIS SESSION, all caught: I claimed a frontmatter tools pattern would scope Bash to one command (it is advisory, and rg can exec arbitrary programs anyway, so the claim was wrong twice); I recommended -c/-l as the low-leak search forms when they are the compilation dump; I wrote an absence rule telling the agent to name the unread remainder with no firewall qualifier, introducing a compilation-leak vector into the very section warning about overclaiming; I relayed a -uu gotcha from the global instructions that is false, then verified it properly only when asked; and earlier I raised a false alarm that live checker topics survived when a crude grep simply could not tell a positive topic from an absent guard. The pattern in every case: a control or claim that reports success without verifying the thing it names.
